learning: Expected: no off-track exit on the oval or s-bend and max_error below 0.06 m. If line loss persists at the tightest bend with max_error still near 0.06 m, the look-ahead is the limit, not the row width. If oscillation is high with max_error low, the outer gain is too high relative to the spread.
notes: Changes from iteration 0's controller: kp 3.0 to 4.0, ki 0.2 to 0.1, kd 0.3 to 0.6. The geometry is the Builder's wider row with weights scaled to 16.7 per metre. The drivetrain and body are unchanged, so the result isolates the sensing and gain change.
rationale: Iteration 0 (the only race so far) failed on all three development tracks. Every run went off track with one line-loss event and max_error of 0.062 to 0.065 m, just over the 0.06 m limit. Progress was 0.53 on the oval, 0.27 on the s-bend and 0.14 on the slalom. The failures happen at the line edge on bends, not from a stall. The Builder's geometry moves the sensor row to ±6 cm at y=0.06 and cuts the weights to 16.7 per metre (±1.0 outer, ±0.5 inner, 0 centre). That gives the robot more warning on sharp bends and lowers the signal gain. The Integrator's concern is that this gain change may be too large. With kp=3 the effective steering gain falls to about 50 per metre, roughly a third of iteration 0's 150, which could leave the robot slow to correct on tight bends. I therefore set kp to 4.0, giving about 67 per metre, so the gain is still lower than iteration 0 (to test the overshoot hypothesis) but not so low that the robot under-steers. ki stays low at 0.1 to avoid wind-up. kd rises to 0.6 to damp the overshoot seen as high oscillation risk. base_speed stays at 1.6 to keep the speed variable unchanged. line_loss stays 'last_direction', which suits a line lost on one side of a bend. Expected result: no off-track exit on the oval and s-bend, with max_error below 0.06 m. If line loss persists, the next step is a longer look-ahead, not a wider row.
